context: Hi! How are you doing today?
I'm doing pretty great! See any good movies lately?
Yes, I've seen some great ones. What about you?
I've seen a few that I really liked. What kind of movies are you into? I'm a horror and comedy fan myself.
I love horror and comedy. I also like action, and recently I have really enjoyed documentaries. Which horror movie is your favorite?

That's a tough one. Honestly I'm a huge fan of earlier horror. I like the new stuff but Nightmare on Elm Street, Wishmaster and Hellraiser.. That era will always be my favorite. See any good ones recently? I've been looking for more modern horror.

I really like those too. I agree that the new ones aren't bad, but nothing beats the classics. Wow, that makes me think of a couple that you'd probably be interested in because of what you said. Do you like sequels at all?
Oh heck yeah. I would argue that Nightmare on Elm Street 3 was the best of the whole bunch. And the remake for IT was downright terrifying.

I know. I also liked the Halloween series. I thought that some of the ones from the 80s were actually better than ones in the 70s. Do you recall who wrote the nightmare on Elm street movies because that'd help me make a recommendation. I think that made a movie recently you'd be interested in
It was Wes Craven. Love that guys work. Sure they were a little campy but It was the way of things at the time.

Have you ever heard of Stephen King? Haha, you said you like horror so that might be a silly question. I forgot about his movies but those were some of my favorites growing up. If you like him, I actually have some really good recommendations.
Bruh. Stephen King is like my favorite author of all time after Orwell.

Hahaha that's crazy. I love Stephen King, and I love Orwell's '1984'. That's crazy. I also think they did a decent job of turning King's books into movies. Which movies based on his books have you seen? I'll know which one to not recommend based on that.

1984 is my exact favorite book actually... As for the King movies IT (Both the 90's one and the remake), Cat's Eye (I think that was him), Pet Cemetery one and two (From back in the day)... Gosh it's been awhile. Gerald's Game. There were a few others but they were all years ago. Fun fact: He used to due the Stan Lee thing where he stuck himself into the movies as a cameo.
That's crazy. 1984 stuck with me for a long time and influenced me a lot. And that is a good fun fact about King hahaha. Now i'm going to have to look that up. Have you ever watched 'The Shining'?
*Facepalm* How do I forget The Shining!? I've seen the one with Jack Nickolson in it. Was there a new one? I cause I would watch that in a heartbeat.
Yes, you have to check out 'Doctor Sleep'. I watched that in 2019 and it's great. It's 'Danny' All grown up.
WHAT? Yes. I absolutely have to go and watch that. Stephen, you tricky monkey. Couldn't just name it 'Shining 2' could he? I'm definitely going to have to watch that.
Yeah haha. You'll get why it's called 'Doctor Sleep' when you see it though. Hey, it was nice talking to you. Have a good day.
You too! Thanks for the movie recommendation.

context.content:
Hello! I'm so excited to talk to you about movies! I'm looking for a movie that is a romantic comedy. I love funny and light-hearted movies. Can you recommend something for me? You: Hi! A romantic comedy sounds like a great choice! To make sure I recommend something you'll love, can you tell me: do you have a preference for a classic movie or something more recent? Please choose the next response based on the user's preference. If the user does not specify, you can ask another question. Choose your response:
A) If the user prefers classic movie, you recommend: Say Hello to Yesterday (1971)
B) If the user prefers classic movie, you recommend: Long Hello and Short Goodbye (1999)
C) If the user prefers recent movie, you recommend: Hello Ghost (2010)
D) Ask the user another question: What kind of tone are you in the mood for? Do you want something light-hearted or a bit more sarcastic? E) Ask the user another question: Have you seen any of the movies in the candidate list before? F) Ask the user another question: What is your favorite actor or actress? G) Ask the user another question: Do you want the movie to be based on a true story? H) Ask the user another question: Do you want the movie to be set in a specific location?
I'm more into horror movies, so I think I might pass on the romantic comedy. But thanks for the suggestion! Do you have any horror movie recommendations?

You can't go wrong with horror movies!  But first, I'd like to know: what type of horror movies do you enjoy? Do you like classic horror, supernatural horror, or something more modern like found-footage horror?
I really enjoy classic horror movies. The atmosphere and storytelling in those older films just have a special charm. Do you have any recommendations for classic horror movies?

I've got just the thing for you. Have you heard of 'Why Horror?' (2014)? It's a documentary that explores the psychology behind why people love horror movies. It's a great choice for a classic horror movie fan like yourself.
That sounds interesting, but I was thinking more along the lines of a classic film from the 30s or 40s. Do you have any recommendations for that era?
I've got a classic horror movie that fits the bill. How about 'Horror House' (1969)? It's a creepy and atmospheric film that's sure to send chills down your spine.
1969 is a bit too recent for my taste. I'm looking for something from the 30s or 40s. Do you have any recommendations from that era?
I have a classic horror movie from the 1930s. How about 'Mad Love' (1935)? It's a psychological horror film that's considered a classic of the genre.
"Mad Love" (1935) sounds perfect! Can you tell me more about it? Like, who directed it and what's the plot about?

'Mad Love' (1935) is a classic horror film directed by Karl Freund, a renowned cinematographer and director. The movie is about a surgeon who becomes obsessed with a woman and decides to transplant her hands onto his lover's body. It's a dark and twisted tale that explores the boundaries of love and obsession. I think you'll really enjoy it!
That sounds intriguing! Could you also tell me if there are any famous actors in the movie? And maybe give me an idea of the runtime?

Peter Lorre stars in 'Mad Love' (1935) as the obsessed surgeon. He gives a chilling performance that's sure to leave you on the edge of your seat. The runtime is approximately 82 minutes. I think you'll find it to be a gripping and unsettling watch.
82 minutes sounds good. I'm definitely interested in watching "Mad Love" (1935). [END]
